title: Lyra FinOps onboarding - SLA & pricing triage

Action items and next steps agreed for follow-up redlines and a pilot benchmark window.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Lopez (Redwood AE); Anika Patel (Redwood SE); Luis Moreno (Redwood CSM); Evan Brooks (CTO, Lyra); Maya Singh (Legal); Tom Rivera (FinOps); Nina Park (Security)

Summary (auto): align on MSA/DPA exceptions, SLA targets, pricing for committed vs burst, KMS/SSO integration plan, pilot benchmarks.

[00:00] Jamie: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll run 50 minutes, agenda is MSA DPA pricing SLA and pilot, feel free to jump in — sorry for the slight echo on my side.
[00:22] Evan: thanks jamie, appreciate it. quick context, lyra is moving a lot of inference to the cloud and we need predictable cost for our triage and therapy-recommendation features. FinOps is worried about a surprise egress and token bills.
[00:40] Tom: yeah we saw a spike last quarter running embeddings for search and the cost math got messy, so main asks: committed pricing option, SLA on latency for primary endpoints, and clear KMS routing for PHI-ish data.
[01:05] Anika: got it, from Redwood's side we offer hosted API and dedicated capacity; dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolated pools, but there's a commitment. We can also provide caching and batching to reduce per-token unit cost.
[01:28] Maya: legal here — we've started redlining the DPA, there are three main items: data residency guarantees, audit log retention, and key custody. we need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed KMS or bring-your-own-key.
[01:47] Jamie: yes we do support customer-managed KMS in the Private tier and options for dedicated where you can supply a key via KMS wrap; I'll confirm the exact flows, mm, sometimes docs say KMS integration but not the HSM detail — i'll follow up.
[02:10] Nina: side question - what's the network egress pathway for dedicated? we need clarity for SOC and firewall rules.
[02:21] Anika: dedicated typically sits in a reserved VPC or peered network; egress depends on the deployment. For private deployments it's customer-controlled egress, for hosted we have standard egress via our cloud provider and can sign egress SLAs as part of the enterprise package.
[02:45] Tom: about SLAs — what uptime and latency SLOs are we talking for the low-latency chat endpoints? our product needs 99.9 for the primary route, and p95 latency under 200ms for short prompts.
[03:03] Anika: we typically aim for 99.9 uptime on Dedicated with an SLA credit model. Latency depends on model and sequence length — we can commit to a p95 latency target for a pinned model and traffic profile in the dedicated pool, but we'll need a benchmark to lock numbers.
[03:28] Evan: ok that matches. On pricing, we need a committed capacity price plus overage bands. Is there a discount ladder for longer commits?
[03:40] Jamie: yes we have monthly and annual reserved capacity tiers; larger commits get deeper discounts. Also, for workloads that are batch-heavy we recommend batching + quantized model variants to lower per-token cost.
[03:55] Tom: does Redwood bill by tokens, by generation-minute, or by inference unit? we need the invoice to map to our internal chargeback.
[04:06] Jamie: primary billing is per-token for text gen and per-embedding unit; for Dedicated we also offer a capacity-style charge (node hours) plus a lower per-token rate. We'll share a sample rate card.
[04:20] Maya: regarding DPA, one concern: subprocessor list — can you provide the cloud infra subprocessors and whether they process the raw inputs or only aggregated telemetry?
[04:35] Luis: good question — we'll send a current subprocessor list; in hosted mode some subprocessors are cloud infra providers and telemetry processors, but we can scope what is stored. Note some model artifacts might be processed transiently in memory only.
[04:55] Evan: pilot scope idea — a two-week dedicated benchmark: 1) chat latency under pinned model, 2) embeddings throughput while ingesting existing search corpus, 3) a failure and fallback test to hosted failover. can Redwood run this in a sandbox?
[05:15] Anika: yes we can spin up a sandbox dedicated pool and run benchmarks with your vectors. We'll need the sample payloads and concurrency patterns (Tom mentioned).
[05:30] Tom: i'll put together the forecast — likely 50 concurrent short-chat users and batch jobs for 10k embeddings per day to start, scaling to 100k in peak.
[05:42] Maya: on legal exceptions, top of mine: encryption-at-rest key ownership, access to raw transcripts for compliance, and indemnity language around model hallucinations.
[06:00] Jamie: for hallucination indemnity we generally have standard clauses — we can discuss carve-outs for specific regulated outputs. For KMS and raw transcripts, Private deployment gives the best control.
[06:18] Nina: security needs: SOC2 attestation, ISO? do you have current certs and penetration-test summary?
[06:28] Luis: we do SOC 2 ISO27001 in progress; I'll attach the latest report and a summary of pen test results.
[06:40] Maya: also retention — Lyra requires 7 years for audit traces in some flows; can you retain audit logs that long?
[06:48] Luis: retention configurable up to 7 years for enterprise customers; storage and cost will be on top of standard retention.
[06:58] Evan: timeline — procurement wants a commercial term by mid-April, legal needs DPA redline turnaround within 5 business days after receiving the redline. can we make that?
[07:12] Jamie: we can try. I'll get the redlines over today/tomorrow; ask your legal to flag must-haves. We'll aim for 2025-04-10 for docs to be back in your hands.
[07:25] Tom: on pricing specifics, what's the overage band? e.g. if we commit 200k tokens/day and we go 20% over during a campaign, what's the rate?
[07:38] Jamie: overage bands are typically our committed rate + 20% for the first band then a higher rate after threshold; i'll include exact numbers in the rate card.
[07:50] Maya: DPA — one more, export controls — Lyra operates in EU+US, need clarity on where model inference occurs and any cross-border flows.
[08:02] Anika: we can pin region routing by policy; model serving can be configured regionally in Dedicated or Private. We'll document the egress paths and region residency options.
[08:20] Evan: question: are you able to run on-prem for fully air-gapped initial POC?
[08:27] Jamie: we have an on-prem/private offering but it requires a longer lead time; possible for enterprise deals, we can scope separately.
[08:38] Tom: procurement specifics — Lyra requires a line item for data residency support and a pass-through for KMS keying costs. Will that be separate on the invoice?
[08:50] Luis: yes these are usually itemized (KMS integration/setup + storage for logs). We'll provide a sample invoice layout.
[09:02] Maya: can you provide a sample SLA credit matrix for downtime? we need to map outage windows to credit percentages.
[09:12] Anika: standard: <99.9 -> 10% credit, <99.5 -> 25%, <99 -> escalated remediation plus credit. But we can review and adjust for enterprise.
[09:28] Evan: good. For the pilot success criteria — define pass/fail: throughput achieved, p95 latency under target, and security gating completed. If pilot fails, we default back to hosted?
[09:44] Anika: yes fallback policies can route to hosted variants; during pilot we usually set up automatic fallback to guarded hosted pools.
[10:00] Jamie: ok wrapping up — action items: Jamie send MSA/DPA redlines; Anika sends pilot plan; Tom sends usage forecast; Maya delivers legal exceptions. We'll reconvene after docs are in.
[10:18] Maya: quick Q: is there a template DPA you can share to speed redlines?
[10:24] Luis: yes i'll attach the template and subprocessor list after the call.
[10:30] Tom: timeline check — procurement internal deadline 2025-04-18, so need to move fast.
[10:38] Jamie: understood, we'll prioritize. Thanks all.
[10:45] Evan: thanks.
[10:48] (crosstalk)
[11:00] End of recording.
